adjudication.rationale: The handler does a non-transactional read of existing attendees (`prisma.booking.findFirst(... include: { attendees: true })`), computes `uniqueGuests` in memory, then performs a separate write (`prisma.booking.update` with `attendees.createMany`). That means concurrent requests can both see the same pre-state and attempt to insert the same guest email(s). However, the finding’s claim that “there is no unique constraint on (bookingId, email)” is not verifiable from this diff (no Prisma schema/migration is shown). If such a constraint exists, the second insert would fail rather than create duplicates. So the concurrency risk is real, but the proposed finding as stated (asserting no unique constraint and definite duplicate insertion) is not strictly provable from the diff alone.
